title: Acts Bible Quiz - Chapter 17
description: Ten questions on Acts 17: Thessalonica and Beroea, and Paul's speech at the Areopagus in Athens.

questions.text: For how many Sabbath days did Paul reason with them from the Scriptures at Thessalonica?
questions.explanation: As was his custom, Paul went in to them and for three Sabbath days reasoned with them from the Scriptures.

answers.text: One Sabbath day
Two Sabbath days
Three Sabbath days
Seven Sabbath days

questions.text: What did the accusers before the rulers of the city say about these men?
questions.explanation: They said that these men acted contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus.

answers.text: That they say there is another king, Jesus, against the decrees of Caesar
That they refuse to pay the tribute that Caesar commands
That they have defiled the temple of the city with Greeks
That they teach the magical arts to the people of the city

questions.text: Whose house was assaulted, and who was dragged before the rulers of the city?
questions.explanation: The crowd assaulted the house of Jason, and when they did not find Paul and Silas, they dragged Jason and certain brothers before the rulers.

answers.text: Dionysius
Damaris
Silas
Jason

questions.text: Why were those at Beroea called more noble than those in Thessalonica?
questions.explanation: They received the word with all readiness of mind and examined the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so.

answers.text: They gave money to the brothers who came
They received the word readily and examined the Scriptures daily
They drove out the Jews from Thessalonica
They built a synagogue for Paul to teach in

questions.text: What provoked Paul's spirit while he waited at Athens?
questions.explanation: His spirit was provoked within him as he saw the city full of idols.

answers.text: He saw that the city was full of idols
A quarrel had arisen among the brothers
There was no synagogue in the whole city
The people of the city were very poor

questions.text: Which philosophers were conversing with Paul?
questions.explanation: Some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers were conversing with him.

answers.text: Pharisees and Sadducees
Epicurean philosophers and Pharisees
Epicurean and Stoic philosophers
Stoic philosophers and scribes

questions.text: What inscription did Paul say he found on an altar in Athens?
questions.explanation: He found an altar with the inscription "TO AN UNKNOWN GOD".

answers.text: TO THE GOD OF ISRAEL
TO AN UNKNOWN GOD
TO ARTEMIS OF THE EPHESIANS
TO JUPITER AND MERCURY

questions.text: What did Paul say about the God who made the world and all things in it?
questions.explanation: He said that this God, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands and is not served by men's hands.

answers.text: He dwells in the temple at Jerusalem and nowhere else
He is served by the hands of priests with sacrifices
He is known to the Jews alone and to no other nation
He does not dwell in temples made with hands

questions.text: What does God now command, according to Paul, and why?
questions.explanation: Paul said God now commands that all people everywhere should repent, because he has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness.

answers.text: That everyone everywhere should repent, for he has appointed a day of judgment
That everyone should be circumcised, for the law still stands
That everyone should keep the feasts that he has appointed
That everyone should sacrifice to him alone in his temple

questions.text: How did the hearers react when they heard of the resurrection of the dead?
questions.explanation: Some mocked, but others said they wanted to hear him again concerning this.

answers.text: They all believed what he had said
They stoned him outside the city
Some mocked, but others wanted to hear him again
The rulers had him arrested at once
